fig01_risk_coverage_test.title: Risk-coverage curves, test
fig01_risk_coverage_test.caption: Risk-coverage curves of every failure detector on the same 997 official test frames; risk is 1 minus the official frame IoU and a frame is bad when its official IoU is below 0.5 (bad rate 29.5%). AURC in the legend. The 4-model ensemble is test-only: every training sequence lies inside some member's training set. The MC row is MC stochastic depth (the segmenter has no dropout layer). Source: results/taskC/failure_detection.json and per-frame scores in work_v2/failure_detection.

fig05_consecutive_frame_iou.title: Consecutive-frame ground-truth IoU
fig05_consecutive_frame_iou.caption: Overlap of the ground-truth instrument masks of consecutive frames in the 15 training sequences (2220 pairs, 1 Hz sampling). Left: distribution, pooled mean 0.323, median 0.272, 76% of pairs below 0.5, against random pairs from the same sequence. Right: per sequence (box = quartiles, whiskers = 1.5 IQR). Source: results/taskK/consecutive_frame_iou.json.

fig07_action_change_distributions.title: Per-action IoU change distributions with the harmful range
fig07_action_change_distributions.caption: Distribution of the per-frame change in instrument IoU produced by each correction action, only for frames the action actually changed (the unchanged share is printed in each panel). The shaded region is the harmful range, a drop larger than 0.01 (the standing harm margin). Top: out-of-fold training frames; bottom: official test frames. Values beyond +-0.4 are clipped into the end bins. The instrument IoU counts a class if it is in the ground truth or the prediction (see Task I). Source: work_v2/actions/*.npz (keys d_A1 .. d_FUSE).

fig08_accuracy_vs_cost.title: Accuracy against cost per policy
fig08_accuracy_vs_cost.caption: Accuracy against cost for every correction policy on the official test set: mean change in instrument IoU on the frames the gate flags (y) against mean latency per frame (x, log scale). Latency is composed from components measured on this machine (RTX 3050 Ti laptop GPU, CPU for the correction steps): the selector and the every-frame fusion rows are the measured M6, M4, M5 latencies of Task 6; routed policies add the measured per-action time on the flagged share of frames; the oracle runs every candidate. Instrument IoU counts a class if it is in the ground truth or the prediction, so most of the A3 gain is removal of invented classes (Task B). Source: results/taskB/policy_table.json, results/task6/final_results.json, work_v2/actions.

fig09_indicator_importance.title: Leave-one-out indicator importance
fig09_indicator_importance.caption: Leave-one-indicator-out importance, out of fold (15 training sequences, gradient-boosted gate, bad frame = instrument IoU below 0.5). Left: the 12-indicator gate, the three disparity indicators in vermillion. Right: the 4 original indicators plus the 6 cross-view indicators (green). Negative bars mean removing the indicator RAISED the AUROC. The cross-view set did not pass its pre-set test (Task D); differences of a few thousandths are within the noise of 15 sequences. Source: results/task4/gate_comparison_gbm.json and results/taskD/decision.json.

fig10_aligner_comparison.title: Aligner comparison for the temporal action
fig10_aligner_comparison.caption: The temporal action (A2) built three ways, mean change in instrument IoU on the frames the gate flags. Whiskers on the two motion-compensated bars are the 95% sequence-clustered interval of their difference from the original (previous mask pasted on unmoved), drawn at the difference added to the original's value; both intervals are of a PAIRED difference. Neither motion-compensated version beat the original; region matching was lower with an interval excluding zero out of fold. Source: results/taskA/aligner_comparison.json.

fig11_memory_starvation.title: Memory starvation per sequence
fig11_memory_starvation.caption: Memory starvation: for every sequence, the share of frames whose gate reliability clears the memory-admission threshold tau_memory = 0.5 (the value the gate was trained and the temporal memory admits with). Frames that do not clear it cannot enter the reliable memory the temporal action draws on. Blue: training sequences (out of fold); vermillion: official test sequences. Source: gate reliability per frame in work_v2/actions/*.npz (key r), threshold from work_v2/release/manifest.json (tau_train).

fig12_metric_ablation.title: Metric-implementation ablation
fig12_metric_ablation.caption: What each definition choice is worth in mIoU points, on the same predictions (the single model, 997 test frames). Reference: the exact official protocol (class 0 never scored, class counted only if in the ground truth, per-frame mean, full 1280x1024). Each bar changes exactly one choice. Two choices (counting a class on the prediction as well, and averaging per class instead of per frame) each move the score by more than 11 points, more than any correction effect in this study. Source: results/taskI/metric_ablation.json.

fig06_reliability.title: Reliability: segmenter before and after temperature scaling, and the gate
fig06_reliability.caption: Calibration. The gate's score against the instrument IoU actually achieved, in 10 equal-count bins of the 997 test frames; the gate is trained to regress this IoU and was not tuned on test. Mean score 0.648 against mean achieved 0.561: the gate over-predicts on the test sequences, most at its highest scores. The segmenter's pixel reliability before and after temperature scaling is not drawn here: results/paper/calibration_pixels.json does not exist yet (tools/calibration_pixels.py needs the GPU). Sources: results/taskC/per_frame_scores.csv.
